Query and joined sessions serve these requests from a configured documents store or the world blob store. Merge Risk: Moderate · previous review ddff0

Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the main change: adding the `documents`/`document` frame pair to the world-session protocol, which matches the shell contract, session serving logic, and SSH shell changes in the summary. It also includes the ticket reference D1-040. It is specific and accurate, so it passes.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** All reviewed changes map to `#3762` objectives. The changed files are pkgs/id/contract/shell-contract.v1.json, pkgs/id/src/shell_contract/tests.rs, pkgs/id/src/world_session/mod.rs, pkgs/id/src/world_session/tests.rs, pkgs/id/src/world_session/types.rs, and pkgs/id/src/world_ssh.rs. The SessionConfig.documents_store field supports the store-threading requirement. The removal of the shell-local document reader and listing code is part of the frame-backed shell requirement. The new tests cover the design's test expectations. No change touches document writes, a replication frame, or the set of public documents, which the issue excludes. The PR description's queue and lane notes are process metadata, not code changes. Scope judgment uses the PR summary and description; I did not re-read the full diff.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** Issue `#3762` is open and directly linked, so its acceptance criteria apply. Met by the reviewed changes: (1) ClientFrame::Documents and ClientFrame::Document, and ServerFrame::Documents (names, next_after, no sequence) and ServerFrame::Document (name, size, text), are added in pkgs/id/src/world_session/types.rs. (2) list_public_documents and read_public_document move into the session layer (world_session/mod.rs) with records-style join-capability authorization and the 64 KiB read cap. (3) The store reaches the session through WorldService's blob store or SessionConfig.documents_store. (4) world_ssh.rs drops the shell-local reader and sends documents, documents_continue, and document frames; the rendered format is kept. (5) shell-contract.v1.json and shell_contract/tests.rs list the new frames. (6) Session tests cover ordering, prefix, exclusive after, reads, refusals, join denied, joined-phase access, and page budget. Not met: `#3762` also requires (a) web contract tests extended and (b) the minimal web list-and-read documents panel from the design (decision 8). The PR description states both are excluded. No web files appear in the reviewed change set. These are concrete unmet coding requirements. The acceptance criterion for overall mcpx/id CI being green in GitHub Actions is not reported. Test results in this assessment are author-reported; I did not run them. **Resolution** Implement the minimal web documents panel (list and read, per design decision 8) and extend the web contract tests in this PR, then re-assess. Alternatively, the maintainers of `#3762` can agree in writing to split the web slice into a new issue. In that case, the web acceptance criteria must be removed from `#3762` or moved to the new issue, and this PR must not use 'Fixes `#3762`' while those criteria remain open. Also confirm that GitHub Actions CI for mcpx/id is green on the PR head.
Full details: Docstring Coverage

**Explanation** Docstring coverage is 50.00% which is insufficient. The required threshold is 80.00%. Docstring coverage is scoped to functions touched by this diff with cyclomatic complexity of at least 2. Documentation-only edits and deletions within surviving functions are included; unchanged diff context and fully deleted functions are excluded. Analyzed 24 functions across 5 files. (1 skipped: 1 unsupported.) **Resolution** Write docstrings for the functions missing them to satisfy the coverage threshold.

# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues
